correctness.rationale: For A=kQ/J² all units form (1+J) ⋊ (k×)^V and the arrowwise commutator formula follows directly from the group law. Every nonzero output arrow requires endpoint separation by at least one of 2r torus labels, forcing a proper support coloring in (q−1)^{2r} colors. Conversely, a coloring chooses labels so at least one linear coefficient is nonzero on each supported arrow; independently choosing the radical entries realizes any target. This establishes necessity and sufficiency, the group derived subgroup, exact lengths, sharp global width, and the disjoint support-weighted count for all q>2. At q=2 the torus vanishes and the unit group is abelian. A standalone independent direct-quotient-product checker exhaustively reproduces seven finite cases and the K5 boundary. Finite checks are supplementary to the written general proof.

originality.rationale: A comparison of implications distinguishes word images and minimal group-commutator lengths from (i) established quiver-algebra structures, (ii) ring-element additive commutator counts, (iii) commuting-pair and unit-order distributions, and (iv) general commutator-width bounds. The exact support-coloring equivalence, complete multiplicity-weighted image-size sum, and unbounded-width family were not covered by inspected claims. An equivalence in older split-metabelian or representation-theoretic literature remains a genuine residual risk, so no claim of exhaustive historical priority is made.
residual_risks: An equivalent support-coloring theorem might be recorded under affine semidirect-product or torus-module terminology in unindexed older literature.
The structural group law is elementary; the originality claim is restricted to the complete sharp coloring, elementwise-length and image-size classification, not the semidirect-product decomposition.

value.rationale: The result determines full iterated commutator word-image strata and the minimum commutator length for every derived-group element in a natural infinite family of finite metabelian groups. The exact chromatic threshold is a structural graph-to-group correspondence, not a restatement of unit class counts, total commutator generation or small-case computations. Complete graphs exhibit unbounded commutator width for fixed q>2; multiplicity-weighted graph-support enumeration gives all image sizes. These are motivated, explicit invariants and a sharp boundary, not an arbitrary slice.
